content.title: About
content.content: A screwdriver is a hand tool designed for inserting and removing screws. Various types exist, including flat‑head, Phillips (cross), Torx (hexalobular), and Pozidriv. The tool typically consists of a steel shaft with a handle made of plastic, wood, or rubber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest documented screwdrivers date back to the late 17th century.
The name comes from the verb “to turn” or “to screw”.
The Phillips cross‑head screwdriver was introduced in the early 20th century by Henry F. Phillips.
Star‑shaped (Pozidriv) screwdrivers became popular in the United States during the 1940s.
Modern screwdrivers often feature magnetic tips to hold screws in place.

items.title: Versatility
items.content: A screwdriver can handle most household and professional tasks, from furniture assembly to electronic repairs.

items.title: Ease of Use
items.content: The tool requires no power source and is easy to store in a toolbox or on a belt.

items.title: Time Saving
items.content: Using the correct screwdriver speeds up assembly and disassembly while reducing the risk of damage.

items.title: Durability
items.content: High‑quality steel shafts and robust handles withstand heavy loads and long service life.

items.title: Safety
items.content: Insulated handles allow work on low‑voltage electrical circuits without shock risk.

items.title: Screw Damage
items.content: Using the wrong size or type can strip the screw head, making it unusable.

items.title: Hand Injuries
items.content: A slippery or broken handle may cause cuts or bruises when force is applied.

items.title: Electrical Shock
items.content: When working on electrical installations, use an insulated screwdriver rated for the voltage.

items.title: Loss of Tool
items.content: Small screwdrivers are easy to misplace; keep them in a dedicated set or holder.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Select a screwdriver with a tip that matches the screw type and size. Insert the tip into the screw slot, apply adequate pressure, and turn clockwise to tighten or counter‑clockwise to loosen. For electronics, use an insulated screwdriver.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store screwdrivers in a dry place, preferably in a compartmentalized toolbox or on a magnetic strip to prevent corrosion. Periodically inspect tip condition and replace worn tools as needed.
